name: MIDI for your DAW
description: A piece written as MIDI for you to finish in your own DAW: the genre researched, a blueprint you approve, every part written and checked on its own channel, and a sketch to hear it by. You get the MIDI: every channel, the whole arrangement, a clip per section, and a cue sheet with your DAW's import steps.

intake.label: Genre
intake.help: As specific as you like: "melodic techno", "neo-soul with Dilla drums", "cinematic hybrid".

intake.label: What's it about?
intake.help: The topic, story or feeling. The music tells it without words.

intake.label: Parts you want
intake.help: e.g. "drums, bass, chords, lead and a counter-melody". The studio picks the rest from the genre.

intake.label: Anything fixed
intake.help: A title, a tempo, a key or a meter you want; the studio chooses the rest.

intake.label: References and must-haves
intake.help: Tracks to study (never copied), progressions or moments you want.

intake.label: MIDI to build on
intake.help: Optional: a .mid with a progression, a riff or a beat of yours. The studio builds around it and keeps it.

steps.name: Genre
steps.describe: The genre researched from 5+ sources: its tempo, lineup, beat grids, harmony, hook traits, and the elements that make it unforgettable.

steps.name: Blueprint
steps.describe: The plan in words, before any note: the hook, tempo, key, chords, one MIDI channel per part, and the story section by section with its intensity.

steps.name: Score and MIDI
steps.describe: Every part written in Strudel on its own MIDI channel, checked (harmony lock, the story's curve) and captured: every channel, the arrangement, a clip per section, the cue sheet.

steps.name: Sketch
steps.describe: Sketch sounds for every channel, auditioned, and a render with stems: so you can hear the notes before they go into your DAW.

steps.name: Your MIDI
steps.describe: You look and listen: the arrangement as a piano roll, the sketch, the cue sheet, and the MIDI pack to download.

checks.title: The genre is researched, not guessed
checks.how: node .claude/skills/music/strudel.mjs genre passes: every field of the profile, 5+ different sources actually read, 5+ unforgettable elements with at least one for the hook and one for the beat, each with a concrete how.

checks.title: The plan holds together
checks.how: node .claude/skills/music/strudel.mjs plan passes: sections contiguous with a function and an intensity, the genre signature uses the profile's elements (hook and beat), the length fits the genre (or the brief), every part on its own channel.

checks.title: The score passes its check and is captured as MIDI
checks.how: node .claude/skills/music/strudel.mjs check ends with 0 problems (harmony locked to the chart, every role playing, nothing past the end, the intensity curve following the sections) and wrote music/notes.json and out/music/midi/.

checks.title: The score holds only the music
checks.how: music/score.strudel.js sets no sounds, effects or gain: notes, velocity and structure only, every part on its role's channel, drums as General MIDI numbers.

checks.title: The owner's own MIDI is kept
checks.how: When the brief brought a .mid (input/), its notes are in the score unchanged (same pitches and rhythm on their own channel), or the note says exactly what was changed and why. n/a when there was none.

checks.title: The MIDI pack is complete
checks.how: out/music/midi/ has the arrangement (<title>-all.mid), one .mid per channel that plays, sections/ with a clip per section, and CUE-SHEET.md with the tempo, key, channels and the import steps; out/music/midi.zip holds all of it.

checks.title: The sketch plays every part
checks.how: strudel.mjs instruments and audition pass, and strudel.mjs render --stems wrote out/music/score.wav with a stem per channel, none silent.
